source.name: A dialog created with keyboard: false must stay open however often Escape is pressed
source.scope: Open upstream bug (https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/43070) at 2bb544eb426e9b1e019c2a98798e0002b8a41d35, unfixed when pinned. Routing Super, then Ultra.

journey.title: Escape must not dismiss a dialog opened with keyboard: false
journey.goal: The confirmation dialog stays open however often Escape is pressed, so the user can still enter the code and send the transfer

functionalJourney.title: Confirm with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking the backdrop does not close the dialog; entering the code and clicking Send completes the transfer

guards.title: Cancel transfer still closes the dialog from the keyboard
guards.goal: Tabbing to Cancel transfer and pressing Enter closes the dialog and records the cancellation

plan.root_cause: The Escape keydown listener in DialogBase only handled non‑modal dialogs, leaving modal dialogs to rely on the native 'cancel' event. Although the cancel listener respected the keyboard: false setting, it stopped preventing the default action after two invocations (observed defaultPrevented:false on the third cancel event), allowing Escape to close the dialog incorrectly.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the Escape keydown listener in DialogBase to always prevent default and then act on the keyboard config: if keyboard is false, simply return (preventing Escape from closing the dialog); if keyboard is true, proceed to hide the dialog. This ensures Escape never triggers the cancel path for modal dialogs, making the behavior independent of the cancel listener's reliability.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will no longer dismiss the confirmation dialog when it is instantiated with keyboard: false, allowing users to enter the OTP and send the transfer without accidental closure. The dialog will remain open until the user explicitly activates the Cancel or Send buttons.
functional_risks: Modal dialogs that rely on Escape to close when keyboard:true will continue to close (behavior unchanged).
Non‑modal dialogs retain their existing Escape handling.

If any custom code depends on the cancel event firing for modal dialogs when Escape is pressed, that event will no longer occur; however, the component's design already treats Escape as a dismissal signal, so impact is minimal.
verification_requirements: Verify that with keyboard:false, pressing Escape does not remove the 'open' attribute from the dialog.
Verify that with keyboard:true, pressing Escape closes the dialog (open attribute removed).
Verify that non‑modal dialogs still respond to Escape according to their keyboard config.
Ensure focus restoration after Escape (when dialog remains open) returns to the triggering button as expected.
Confirm that the Cancel and Send buttons still function correctly after Escape presses.
